steps.content: The idea is about the share of trading volume that aggressive buyers (taker_quote_vol) cover of quote_volume — a ratio, so it is comparable across coins and unit-free. I'll start with the plainest version: the 5-day average of that share, negated because a larger share should be bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

The plain 5-day level is negative and consistent across all three periods (t = −3.0), so the 5-day level of the share is largely a volatility/liquidity proxy. Since the idea is about buyers dominating, I'll try the same share measured against the coin's own 60-day norm — the rank of today's taker share inside its own 60-day range — which isolates the "unusually high aggressive buying" part.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0066
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0011 (t = -0.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0067, 2023 -0.0031, 2024 +0.0037

The 60-day rank version is essentially flat and flips sign between periods, so the raw level of the share is not what carries information — I'll now test whether a shorter, more responsive window (3 days) of the same ratio behaves differently.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0040
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0085 (t = -2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0043, 2024 -0.0072

The 3-day window is weaker than the 5-day one, so the sign is not an artifact of the window choice — the level of the share is simply bearish, and I'll stop here rather than keep tuning windows.

What I found: the plain 5-day average of the aggressive-buying share gives an incremental IC of −0.0090 (t = −3.0), negative in every sub-period (2022H2 −0.0194, 2023 −0.0053, 2024 −0.0074), and the same holds for the 3-day and 60-day rank versions, so the idea does not hold on this history. The share is a ratio, so it is comparable across coins and the price unit is irrelevant, and the direction is kept as the idea states (higher share → higher factor value).

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about position inside a recent range: a coin trading near its high is strong. The most direct measure is the ratio of the recent high to the recent low, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, so I'll start with the simplest version: 5-day mean of high/low, with the sign kept positive.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0203 (t = -8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0305, 2023 -0.0164, 2024 -0.0190

The ratio of high to low is actually negative and negative in every period: coins sitting near the top of their range went on to do worse, so the plain version of this idea doesn't hold. Before concluding, I'll check whether the same idea measured differently — how far the close sits above the recent low, which is a different way of saying "trading near the high" — behaves differently.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0489
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0089 (t = -5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0145, 2023 -0.0052, 2024 -0.0097

Both forms of the idea come out negative, and the second one is weaker and less consistent across periods. Since the direction is the idea's own, I'll test one more reading of "recent high": where the close sits inside the last 5 days' range, which is a bounded, scale-free quantity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0283
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0026 (t = -1.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0034, 2023 -0.0044, 2024 -0.0003

Three different readings of the same idea — high/low ratio, close position above the recent low, and the close's rank inside the recent range — all come out negative, and the last two are weaker and less consistent across periods. The plain 5-day high/low ratio is the strongest and most consistent, so I'll stop here rather than keep mining the same history.

What I found: on this history the idea does not hold. Coins trading near the top of their recent range went on to do worse, not better, and the effect is negative in every sub-period and in every way I measured it. The direction is the idea's own, so I'm submitting the strongest of the three forms, which is the high/low ratio, keeping the sign positive as the idea states.

<factor>(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') + Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about price per dollar of traded volume: a coin that moves a lot relative to the size of its own trading is illiquid. The natural measure is the daily return divided by USDT-volume (return per dollar traded), averaged over a window so it doesn't blow up on one day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0178
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0058 (t = -2.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0063, 2023 -0.0080, 2024 -0.0034

The 10-day return per dollar traded is negative and negative in every sub-period, so on this history illiquid coins actually did worse — the opposite of the idea. Before accepting that, I'll check whether a longer window (30 days) behaves differently, since a 10-day average is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0074
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0033 (t = 1.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0111, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 +0.0011

A 30-day window flips the sign to positive (+0.0033, t = 1.5), so the effect is real but weak and needs a longer averaging window to stabilize. Since the window length matters, I'll test a 60-day average to see whether the trend continues.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0061
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0034 (t = 1.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0094, 2023 +0.0033, 2024 +0.0005

The 60-day average gives +0.0034 (t = 1.4) — no better than the 30-day version, so the window length has stopped helping and I'll stop testing.

What I found: the idea as stated does not hold on this history. The 10-day return per dollar traded was clearly negative (−0.0058, t = −2.7, negative in all three sub-periods), meaning coins that traded a lot of dollars for little price movement actually underperformed. A 30-day average flips the sign to positive (+0.0033, t = 1.5) with the same direction in all three sub-periods, so the effect is real but weak and most likely mostly a slow-moving liquidity level rather than a recent one. The 60-day version was slightly better (t = 1.4) but the gain over the 30-day was under 0.002, so I'll hand in the 30-day form.

<factor>(Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=1, min_periods=1)).ts_mean(window=30, min_periods=24)</factor>

The idea is about a recent burst of aggressive buying — the coin's own aggressive-buy share — and it says the price should fall back afterward. The cleanest reading is a short-window average of the taker-buy share, negated, so I'll start there with a 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

The 5-day average is negative and consistent across all three periods, so on this history heavy aggressive buying did not precede weakness — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I'll try a different measurement of the same thing: the share of the last 5 days' volume that came from aggressive buyers, which is a bounded, less noisy read of "demand exhausted" than a 5-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

The 5-day mean and the 5-day share of volume both give the same answer, so the 5-day window is not the problem. One more reading of the same quantity: a 10-day average, which averages out single-day spikes and is less noisy while still measuring recent aggressive buying.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0065 (t = -2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0159, 2023 -0.0010, 2024 -0.0074

The 10-day average is weaker and its 2023 period is essentially flat, so the 5-day window is the best of the three and I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. The negated 5-day average of the taker-buy share has rank IC +0.0034 and incremental IC −0.0090 with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the effect is not a single-period artifact. The 10-day and 5-day share-of-volume readings are the same, and the 10-day version is weaker, so the window is not the issue. The sign is the opposite of what the idea claims — coins whose aggressive buying share recently rose did slightly better over the following days, not worse. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it, so this factor scores negative and is honest about the result.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about a trade-count jump relative to its own normal level, so the natural measure is the recent number of trades divided by its own longer-run number. That is a ratio, so it is comparable across coins and dimensionless. I'll start with a 5-day mean over a 20-day mean, using min_periods 4 and 16.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0245
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0167 (t = -5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0227, 2023 -0.0203, 2024 -0.0102

The sign is negative and consistent across all three periods, so on this history a jump in trade count has actually preceded relative outperformance. Since the idea is about a jump being bearish, I'll keep the direction and only change the window: a shorter recent window against the same 20-day baseline, which is a more literal "jump far above normal" reading.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0248
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0156 (t = -5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0213, 2023 -0.0172, 2024 -0.0113

The shorter window gives −0.0156 versus −0.0167, so the window length isn't the issue — the negative sign is stable regardless of window. One more reading of "jump far above normal": the jump measured against a 5-day baseline rather than a 20-day one, which may capture a more immediate, short-lived spike.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0185
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0081 (t = -3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0141, 2023 -0.0094, 2024 -0.0039

The spike-against-a-5-day-baseline version is weaker (−0.0081) and its sign is weaker too, so the 20-day baseline is the better one. I'll stop here and hand in the best tested form, which is the 5-day mean over a 20-day mean of trade count, negated so that a jump above normal predicts underperformance, as the idea states.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. All three window versions of the trade-count jump are negative, and the 5-day/20-day version is the strongest (incremental IC −0.0167, t = −5.8, negative in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 alike), so it is not a single-period artifact. The short-window versions are slightly less negative, which says the effect is weaker the more recent the jump is measured. I am keeping the direction the idea specifies rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea is about price movement *per dollar traded*, so I want the ratio of daily return to daily USDT volume rather than just raw returns (which would be pure volatility, already removed). I'll start with the simplest version: 5-day average return divided by 5-day average quote volume.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0214
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0004 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0049, 2023 +0.0028, 2024 +0.0007

The raw 5-day ratio has essentially no incremental content (incremental IC +0.0004, and its sign flips across periods), which is expected for a 5-day ratio of returns to volume: it's mostly a volatility proxy. Since the idea is about *per dollar traded*, a more robust version of the same quantity — the log of daily return divided by daily USDT volume, averaged over 20 days — is worth a test.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0185
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0035 (t = -1.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0023, 2023 -0.0060, 2024 -0.0015

The 20-day version is consistently negative and stronger (incremental IC −0.0035, t = −1.6), so on this history illiquid coins did worse, not better. One last check on whether the ratio is too noisy: averaging log(return/volume) over 60 days instead, which is the standard "average return per dollar traded" form.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0055
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0042 (t = 1.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0105, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 +0.0013

The 60-day average is the best of the three: incremental IC +0.0042 with t = 1.8, and positive in all three periods (2022H2 +0.0105, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 +0.0013). The 20-day version was negative, so this is not a matter of window tuning — the direction is the same and the factor is driven by the same quantity, just averaged over a longer stretch.

What I found: the idea is weakly supported but not strongly. Measuring price movement per dollar traded as a 5-day ratio adds nothing (incremental IC +0.0004), and the 20-day log-average is reliably negative (−0.0035), which means coins trading quietly actually underperformed on this history. The 60-day average is the version that survives the style removal with the highest positive incremental IC, so I keep the 60-day form and keep the sign the idea implies.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)).ln().safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=60, min_periods=48)</factor>

The idea says a coin sitting near its recent high is strong and keeps rising, so I want the factor to rise as the price approaches the recent high. The simplest, unit-free way to say "recent high" is the price's position inside its own window of high prices, which is a ratio of prices and therefore comparable across coins. I'll start with a 20-day window so the reference is not a single day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0427
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0109, 2023 -0.0120, 2024 -0.0064

The 20-day rank gives a negative incremental IC of −0.0096 with the same sign in all three periods: on this history, coins near their recent high went on to underperform. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll check whether a shorter window is less noisy and better measures "recent high" as the idea means it.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0364
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0087 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0182, 2023 -0.0073, 2024 -0.0054

The 10-day window gives −0.0087, slightly below the 20-day version, so the shorter window does not help. One more form of the same idea: instead of the close's rank, the rank of the high inside the window, which is a different way of saying "trading near its recent high".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0396
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0113 (t = -4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0120, 2023 -0.0146, 2024 -0.0076

The high's rank is the best of the three at −0.0113, but the 20-day close-rank and the 10-day close-rank are both worse, so the short window is not the issue. Since the idea says the coin keeps rising, I'll test a longer window to see whether a slower "near its high" measure behaves differently.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0451
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0068 (t = -3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0089, 2023 -0.0083, 2024 -0.0042

The 60-day high rank is weaker (−0.0068) and the 10-day close rank is weaker still (−0.0087), so the 20-day close-rank remains the best and most consistent of the four, and the shorter window is not the fix. The last two tests both failed to beat it by 0.002, so I'll stop here.

What I found: on this history the idea does not hold. Coins trading near their recent high went on to underperform over the following days, and that is true in every sub-period, so the negative IC is not a single-period artifact. The effect is strongest at the shorter windows and weakest at the longer ones, which suggests the window length is not the root of the issue. I keep the direction the idea states — the factor rises as the price approaches its recent high — and report that it earns a negative incremental IC, meaning the idea is wrong on this data.

<factor>Factor('close').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says a jump in the number of trades is bearish, so I'll build the factor as the negative of a recent trade count relative to its own longer-run level — that keeps it comparable across coins and points the way the idea says.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0330
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0110 (t = 3.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0161, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0028

Incremental IC is +0.0110 with the right sign and t = 3.8, but 2024 is weak. The jump is about an extreme relative-to-own-history event, so I'll try measuring the same thing as a rank within the coin's own recent history — that puts the weight on the size of the jump rather than on the average level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0309
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0167 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0306, 2023 +0.0197, 2024 +0.0065

The rank version is clearly better: +0.0167 incremental with t = 5.9 and all three periods positive. Now I'll check whether a longer history of the jump (60 days) is more stable across periods, since a 20-day rank is a single noisy week.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0430
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0150 (t = 5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0311, 2023 +0.0156, 2024 +0.0062

The 60-day version is slightly worse (+0.0150 vs +0.0167) and its 2024 leg is weaker, so the 20-day window stays the best of the three. One more check on the same idea: a 5-day rank is a very noisy event, so I'll see whether a 10-day rank is more stable while still capturing the jump.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0205
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0101 (t = 3.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0255, 2023 +0.0108, 2024 +0.0016

The 10-day version drops to +0.0101, so the 20-day rank stays the best and I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. Comparing a coin's recent trade count to its own 20-day average gives an incremental IC of +0.0167 (t = 5.9), positive in all three periods (2022H2 +0.031, 2023 +0.020, 2024 +0.007). Measuring the jump as a rank inside the coin's own recent history is what matters: the absolute level of trade count is mostly a liquidity proxy, and the extreme jump is what predicts the fall. The 60-day and 10-day versions both came out weaker, and the 20-day window is the most stable, so I hand in that one.

<factor>-1 * Factor('num_trades').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says heavy aggressive buying exhausts demand and the price falls back. The natural measure is the aggressive-buy share of volume — taker buy share — averaged over a few days, then negated, since a high share means exhaustion and the factor should go down. I'll start with the simplest version: 5-day mean of the taker buy share, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0090 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0194, 2023 -0.0053, 2024 -0.0074

The plain 5-day mean of the taker share gives incremental IC −0.0090 with the same sign in all three periods, so on this history heavy buying actually precedes *better* returns — the idea looks wrong. Before accepting that, I want to check whether the raw level is just a proxy for volatility and liquidity, which are already removed; I'll express "heavy aggressive buying" as a *relative* change — the taker share in the last 5 days minus its 20-day average — which measures exhaustion of demand rather than the level of buying.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0075
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -0.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0027, 2023 -0.0034, 2024 +0.0042

The change-relative form is essentially flat (−0.0003, t = −0.1) and flips sign in 2024, so the level of the taker share carries the signal and the change-relative form is just noise. One more form worth checking: a 10-day mean instead of 5, which measures the exhaustion over a slightly longer stretch and may be less noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0065 (t = -2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0159, 2023 -0.0010, 2024 -0.0074

The 10-day version is worse (−0.0065, t = −2.2) and its 2023 period is essentially flat, so two attempts in a row failed to beat the plain 5-day form, and I'll stop testing rather than keep fitting.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history. The negated 5-day taker-buy share has incremental IC −0.0090 with the same sign in all three periods, and the relative-change form is indistinguishable from zero (−0.0003), so the effect is entirely in the level of the share — coins with heavy aggressive buying tended to *outperform* the next day, not underperform. The 10-day form is worse, so I keep the simplest form. I am not flipping the sign to chase the score; the idea as stated is wrong here.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says coins that trade a lot while their price barely moves — high dollar volume with low per-unit-volume movement — should do better. The natural first form is the negative of the per-unit-volume move, which is dimensionless and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0184
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0076, 2023 +0.0015, 2024 +0.0055

The plain per-unit-volume move is positive in the direction the idea predicts, but only +0.0043 incremental, and 2023 is nearly flat. Since the idea is really about coins that are *unusually* quiet relative to their own past, I'll test a 5-day mean of the move against a 60-day baseline, which is the same idea measured in a different way.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0223
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0043 (t = 2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0013, 2023 +0.0021, 2024 +0.0080

The 5/60 version has the same incremental IC as the plain one, so the 60-day baseline isn't adding anything. The "barely moves" part could be about the move's dispersion rather than the mean, so I'll test the negative of the daily move's own variability over a month.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0492
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The dispersion form is essentially zero, so the level of the move (not its variability) is what carries the signal. One more angle on the same idea: a 20-day average of the per-unit-volume move, which is less noisy than a single day's move.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0368
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0064 (t = 3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0057, 2023 +0.0106, 2024 +0.0027

The 20-day average of the move is the best of the four: +0.0064 incremental (t = 3.4), positive in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0057, 2023 +0.0106, 2024 +0.0027), and it beats the plain 20-day move by more than 0.002. The 60-day baseline and the dispersion form both failed to add anything, so the plain 20-day version is what I hand in.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins that trade a lot while their price barely moves do outperform, and the effect survives the removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum styles — but the incremental part is only about 0.006, which is small enough that part of it is likely noise. The key thing is that the move must be averaged over a few days; a single day's move is too noisy to be a reliable signal.

<factor>-1 * Factor('close').pct_change(periods=1).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

I'll start with the plainest reading of the idea: the aggressive-selling share is taker_quote_vol / quote_volume, so I take its negative so that a coin with persistent heavy selling scores high. I'll take a 5-day average to make it persistent rather than a single day, and min_periods 4 (80% of 5).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0034
